content.text: Stephen Brice, a Union supporter in St. Louis, refuses to enlist because he must support his widowed mother, while Richter, Tiefel, and Tom Catherwood join the Union forces. Camp Jackson’s secessionist militia is captured by Lyon on May 10, sparking riots and deepening divisions. Stephen saves John Brinsmade during the violence and meets Ulysses Grant outside the Arsenal. Virginia Carvel remains devoted to Confederate cousin Clarence, though she increasingly admires Stephen. Refugees, wounded soldiers, poverty, confiscations, and martial law transform St. Louis. Eliphalet Hopper exploits Colonel Carvel’s financial distress and later threatens Virginia, but Stephen protects her. Stephen eventually joins the Union army, serves under Sherman, fights at Vicksburg, rescues Clarence by arranging his transport north, and later becomes a major on Sherman’s staff. At Judge Whipple’s office, Virginia and Stephen’s affection becomes undeniable, while her father secretly returns there from the South. Whipple dies peacefully as Virginia plays “Lead, Kindly Light.” In 1865, Stephen meets Grant and Lincoln at City Point.
